name: en_chinmaya_day03
transcript: Sahana bhavato sahano bhunakto sahaviryam karavavahai te Jasvinavadhitamastuma vidvishavahai Om Shanti Shanti Shanti Om Yam Brahma Varunendra Rudra anti devyastavaih vedaih sangapadakramopanishadaih gayanti samsaragah dhyanavati Sthita yasyam tam na vidu surasuraganah devayat devayat So in the first chapter, Arjuna gives all the reasons why they should not fight the war. He almost collapses on the chariot. Bhagwan uses some lashing words to wake him up. Arjuna again repeats the same arguments. How can I fight with my teacher, with the elders? I think it is better to beg and live than kill these noble ones. But then Arjuna himself realizes that there is a deep confusion within. What is dharma, what is adharma, what is right, what is wrong, what should be done, what should not be done. He realizes his confusion, but one great thing Arjuna does is, he completely surrenders unto Bhagwan. The first chapter is called Arjuna Vishada Yoga. Now a question may come, how can Vishada be considered Yoga? Vishada means sorrow. Yoga is a science of uniting with the Lord. How can sorrow be considered a yoga? But then the answer given is, it is because of this sorrow that Arjuna surrendered unto Bhagwan. It is because of this sorrow that Arjuna sought this greatest knowledge. So therefore, even this sorrow, is a blessing in disguise. Even this sorrow is an auspicious beginning. It is not inauspicious, though superficially it may appear to be inauspicious. So even this vishada is considered to be yoga because vishada opens up the door. towards yoga. So then Arjuna surrenders completely to Bhagwan, saying Bhagwan, I am absolutely helpless. Though I have all the talents and abilities to fight the war, but these talents I am not able to bring it out. because of utter helplessness, born out of confusion regarding what is dharma and what is adharma. So therefore Bhagwan, nishchitam shreyah, whatever it is, please tell me. Whatever is ultimately good for me, ultimately good for all. For all times, whatever it is, please tell me, please guide me. Shishyasteham shadhimaam tvam prapannam. I completely surrender unto you. I am your disciple. I don't know anything. Please teach me. I want this knowledge because the sorrow which I am experiencing now, this sorrow can never go with any kind of external. adjustments. I may be given the Lordship over the entire heaven, over all the gods. I may be given a kingdom which is unrivaled and prosperous, but even then this sorrow which is burning, all my senses, this sorrow will not go away. So Bhagwan, please teach me, please guide me. Saying this, Arjuna kept quiet, saying I am not going to fight. Na yotsye. So now, what does Bhagwan do? Let us chant the next verse. Tamu vacha Rishi Keshah prahasanniva Bharata. Senayorubhayor madhye vishidantamidam vachaha. So now this is the condition of Arjuna, he is quiet. He's determined not to fight and he has sought for the highest knowledge. Now Bhagwan looking at this condition of Arjuna. What is the condition of Arjuna? Senayor ubhayor madhye vishidantam. The middle of the two armies. What is the condition of Arjuna? Vishidantam, drowning in sorrow. Looking at him. Bhagwan Rishikeshah, the master of the senses, the supreme Lord, prahasan iva, smilingly. smilingly idam vachah uvacha. Bhagwan spoke these words. Now see the condition here. On one side Arjuna is grieving, crying, on the other side Bhagwan is smiling. Situation is the same. You just see how Two different people are reacting to the same situation. One is crying, other is smiling. Now a question may come, why is Bhagwan smiling? Prahasanniva, prahasan means smiling. Now the question may come, why Bhagwan is smiling? The answer comes in the next verse actually. But there can be so many reasons why Bhagwan is smiling. Reason number one. Just bring into the picture how Arjuna entered into the war field. What did he say? Bhagwan, take the chariot. into the center field. The center of the two armies. Let me see how many people have come to fight. Who all have come to fight. Now at that time he was full of confidence, courage, fearlessness, bold. This was the Arjuna who entered into the battlefield. Now what is the condition of Arjuna? Totally grieving and crying. There's a stark contrast between the Arjuna who entered into the field and now the condition of Arjuna. It is something like You know, during Diwali days, you have these firecrackers. So there's a huge bomb or some big firecracker. So everybody is expecting something huge. Horrible sound everybody is expecting. So now you light that firecracker. So you have that string. So now it has caught fire. Now the sparks are coming. Everyone has run away from there. Some of them have closed their ears also. And then what happens? Some sounds, gone. Isn't it? This is the condition of Arjuna. World number one warrior coming there to fight and now it is crying. I will not fight. This may be one reason why Bhagwan smiled. Another reason why Bhagwan smiled is because as we all know, Arjuna is a very close friend of Bhagwan. So here was this Arjuna throughout his life, he was running around for so many kinds of vidyas. Dhanurvidya, Astravidya, Shastravidya, throughout his life he was busy acquiring varieties of vidyas including Gandharva Vidya. He got this Gandharva Vidya the knowledge about science, I mean what is that? music, dance, etcetera. He got it from Swargaloka. His teacher was Chitrasena. He knows how to dance, how to play tabla, mritangam, everything he knows. So throughout his life he was busy with all kinds of apara vidyas. Now for the first time, he is showing interest in Paravidya or Atma Vidya or Brahma Vidya. So Bhagwan was very happy. This might be another reason why Bhagwan is smiling. You want your loved ones to gain the highest, to gain the best. Very many times it happens. The husband or the wife attend satsang, they are attending all Gita classes, but their spouse is just the opposite. Husband is there in the class, wife just doesn't like it. Or wife loves this kind of spiritual discourses, husband is just the opposite. Very rarely we find husband and wife together liking this. So very many times what happens is, The one person who loves this, who knows this value, wants the beloved also to gain this knowledge because this is the best, isn't it? So now Bhagwan, because his dearest friend is Arjuna, Bhagwan smiles because he was happy that at least now he's showing interest. in this knowledge. This is another reason why Bhagwan might have smiled. There can be one more reason also. What is that reason? When the patient comes to the doctor, crying, weeping, anxious, worried, describing his physical problems. Not knowing what to do, not knowing what kind of disease he's suffering from. And as this patient is describing the symptoms, the diseases of the body. The doctor as he's listening to these, when the doctor comes to know that, oh, this person is suffering from this, what will the doctor do? The doctor will smile, isn't it? Why that smile? The problem with which he's suffering from, I have the solution. When you have the solution, you smile. When you don't have the solution, you weep. So here is Arjuna weeping and crying because he doesn't know the solution. Here is Bhagwan smiling because he knows what Arjuna is going through. He exactly knows what solution alone can solve this Arjuna disease. That may be one more reason why Bhagwan is smiling. Anyway, Bhagwan smiled and he spoke these words. Now from the next words onwards, real Teaching of Bhagavad Gita starts. Bhagwan starts with a powerful verse, a very, very famous verse. Let us chant verse number 11. Shri Bhagavanuvacha, Ashochyananvashochastvam. Prajnavadaancha bhashase gataasu nagataasuccha nanu shochanti panditaah Yes. Bhagavad Gita begins with a bang, as they say. What is that bang? Bhagwan smiles, and this is one reason why Bhagwan smiles. Arjuna, actually Bhagwan is making fun of Arjuna. Arjuna, tvam anva shochah, you are grieving. A shochyan, you are grieving for the ungrievable, for those whom. You should not grieve for Ashochyan. You are grieving for the ungrievable. At the same time, on one side you are grieving, on the other side Prajnavadascha bhashase. You are speaking the words of wisdom. You are speaking like a wise man. So on one On one side you are speaking like a wise man, on the other side you are grieving. Look at that contrast. Arjuna, shall I tell you one thing? Panditaha na anushochante. The sign of the Wise. The indications of the wise, the sign of wisdom is the wise man never grieves. Gatasun agatasun with regard to gata asun. Gata asu, asu means prana. Life breath is called asu. So gata asu means what? Those from whom the life breath has gone away, meaning dead people. Gatasun, dead people, Agatasun. Agatasun means what? Not yet dead. still breathing or dying or living. With respect to the living people or non-living people, Panditaha na anushochanti, the wise people don't grieve. This is the sign of wisdom. So what is the sign of wisdom? Absence of grief is the sign of wisdom. Absence of sorrow is the sign of wisdom. Peace, happiness, cheerfulness is the sign of wisdom. Arjuna, In your case, it is very clear. On one side you are speaking as though you are a wise man, on the other side what are you doing? You are crying. What does it mean? It simply means you are otherwise, not wise. It simply means whatever you are saying is wrong. A person who is wise, he will have right understanding about life. And because he has right understanding about life, his analysis about life situation will be perfect, it will be right. He will have right analysis of the situations of life, of the problems, of the challenges of life, his analysis will be perfect. And because of perfect analysis, his decisions will be perfect. And because of perfect decisions, his actions will be perfect. And those people who perform perfect actions can never grieve. A person with right understanding about life will have right analysis. Right analysis will lead to right decisions. Right decisions will lead to right actions. For such people who perform right actions, where is the question of grief? Such a person alone can be peaceful in this world, happy in this world. Arjuna, the very fact that you are grieving shows your knowledge is imperfect. Your analysis is imperfect. Your decision is imperfect. Your actions are imperfect. The beauty of the verse is, Bhagwan is here a perfect teacher. What is the job of the teacher? The job of the teacher is, place the finger exactly where it pains, where the problem is. Pinpoint the mistake. This is the job of the teacher. The shishya is wrong somewhere because of his wrong judgements, wrong knowledge, he is suffering. What is the job of the teacher? Where exactly are you wrong? But the first step is to prove that the shishya is wrong. My dear Arjuna, you are wrong. What is the proof? The very, the very fact that you are crying proves that you are wrong. Now Bhagwan is going to explain why Arjuna is wrong, where Arjuna has made the mistake. The term used here is Panditaha. Na anushochanti. The wise people, they don't grieve. Now the common meaning which is prevalent in the society regarding Pandita is some priest in temple. Whenever we hear the term Pandit, We think some priest in the temple. So here Bhagwan Shankaracharya as he makes it very clear who is a pandita. Panda, atma vishaya buddhihi yasyam. Te panditah. Those who have Panda is called Pandita. Now what is this Panda? Panda means the knowledge about the self. Those who know who they are, that knowledge about the supreme self is called Panda, and those who have Panda, they are called as Pandita. So now what is Bhagwan trying to indicate, Arjuna? All your sorrow is because you don't know who you are. All your sorrow is because of a mistaken identity with regard to yourself. So if you want to put an end to your sorrow, there is only one way, know thyself. This is the message. Now, very interestingly, Bhagwan Shankaracharya has not written any commentary up to 10th verse. First chapter Bhagwani, silence, second chapter up to 10th verse, Bhagwan Shankaracharya has not written any commentary, but after this, he writes a huge commentary. Summarizing what is the problem with which Arjuna is suffering. Now let us discuss that point. The first mistake we all commit is Ignorance with regard to our own true nature. Everything starts from agnana. What is our true nature? We are Sat, Chit, Anand. We are existence, consciousness, bliss. This is our true nature. Sat means existence. Chit means consciousness. Anand means bliss. This is our true nature. But when we don't know our true nature, that ignorance of our true nature is called agyanam. Agyanam. Not agnanam with regard to the worldly knowledge, no. Agnanam regarding our own true identity. All problems starts from here. Agnanam. I don't know who I am. So what is the next? So from this mistake, what is the next mistake we commit? Naturally, I want to know who I am. So now I start using inference. Through my own superficial analysis of my life, I try to. Know myself, understand myself. So what do I do? I look upon myself and what do I find? Whatever is happening in this body, I am able to experience. Whatever is happening outside this body, I am not able to experience. Therefore, I am limited to this body. See this. If there is a pain in this body, I am able to experience. If there is a pain in somebody's body, I am not able to experience. Therefore, this body is mine, that body is not mine. Whatever is within the limitations, within the boundaries of this body, I am experiencing it. Whether it is heat or cold, whether it is joy or sorrow, within the boundaries of this body I am experiencing, outside the boundary I am not experiencing. So what is my limit? My limit is this body. Now slowly, slowly I start defining myself as this body. Not only my direct experience, but by inference also, I try to define myself as this body. How? Somebody is born. Somebody is born means what? Physical body is born. And now that person is available for interaction in this world, and the physical body is dead, that person is no more available for interaction. What does it mean? That person exists with the existence of that body, that person no more exists with the non-existence of that body. This I see in others. I'm not seeing in myself. I'm seeing in others. So with the existence of the body, that person is existing, with the non-existence of the body, that person is no more existing. Therefore the same thing should be true with me also. Meaning what? I exist with this body, I die with this body. Therefore, I am this body. This is called inference. So how do I define myself? I define myself as this body. This is the second mistake coming from the primary mistake. What is the first mistake? Ajnanam, I don't know myself, I want to know myself, so how do I define myself? I define myself as the body. I am the body. This is called Dehatma Bhava. Deha itself is Atma, body itself is me, that is called Dehatma, Dehatma Bhava. So this understanding comes now. I am the body. This is the second step. Now, what kind of desires we will have? Our desires will always be based on our true nature. What is our true nature? Sat Chit. Ananda is our true nature, based on that true nature alone we will have desire. So what will be our desire? Our desire will be to exist. All of us we want to exist. We don't want to die. We want to live. From where did the desire come from? The desire has come because our Atma, the supreme self is Sat. Sat means existence. That which is always existing. That which can never become non-existent, that is the nature of the self and that is actually my nature. So, I will always have the desire to exist, but now my definition of myself is I am the body. So what will be my definition of existence? As long as the body exists, I exist, so let me protect the body. Let me preserve the body. Let me do everything to live ever and ever in the body. Isn't it? Let me not grow old. Let me do everything at least to postpone old age if not prevent. Everything I will do because my definition of myself is this body. So I will try to exist through the body. I will try to experience happiness. Now again this is another desire. What is the desire? I want to be happy forever and ever and ever. Where did this desire come from? It has come from my true nature. What is my true nature? Ananda Swarupa is my true nature. I am Sachit Ananda. Infinite bliss is my true nature. Happiness is my true nature. So naturally I will try to desire happiness. But now since my definition of myself is the body, so what kind of happiness will I seek? I will seek happiness through the body. I will seek happiness of the body. Anything which makes the body comfortable, happy, cheerful, that I will do. How will I get the knowledge? Chit means consciousness, chit means knowledge also. So I will try to grab all that knowledge, I will try to gain all that knowledge which will give me sat. which will give me Anand. Because I want to exist forever, I want to exist happily forever, I want to exist with infinite happiness, infinite joy, infinite peace. This is what I desire, but the mistake is I will keep on desiring it in and through the body because I consider myself as the body. Now, so what is the first step? Ajnana. What is the next one? Dehatma bhava. With the dehatma bhava. Now that you consider yourself to be the body, now that you consider your existence. as nothing but the existence of the body, naturally the third step will come. The third step is raga. Raga means attachment. You'll be attached to the body. Why are you attached to the body? Because it is this body which is giving me existence. It is this body which is giving me happiness. And therefore, since I am craving for existence and happiness, and it is this body which is giving me Therefore, naturally what will happen? There will be raga, that is the third one. Raga means attachment. Primary raga is with the body, secondary ragas is with everything connected to the body which will give me security, which will give me happiness. So therefore, I will have attachment not only with the body, I will also have attachment to everything connected to the body which gives the body happiness, which gives the body existence. So what are they? It can be wealth. It can be power, it can be position, it can be relatives, it can be house, everything. But they are all secondary attachments. What is the primary attachment? The body. They are all there, they are capable of giving happiness to this body. They are capable of giving security to this body, therefore they are lovable. So what comes? Raga comes. What is raga? Attachment. Now wherever there is raga, there has to be dwesha. You can't avoid it. Raga means what? Likes. Dwesha means dislikes. You like something, someone or some situation because it is capable of giving happiness to you. You don't like something, someone, or some situation because they give sorrow to you. Raga and Dwesha, they are the two sides of the same coin. You cannot have only Raga, no Dwesha, impossible. Greater the intensity of raga, equally great will be the intensity of dwesha. If you want to get rid of raga, you will have to get rid of dwesha also. Raga dwesha, they always come in pairs. So what are the steps now? Number one, agnana. Number two, dehatma bhava. Number three, raga dwesha. Now what happens when the mind is filled with raga dwesha? So what is raga dwesha? I am attached to everything that gives me security and happiness and comfort and peace. I am repelled by everything that threatens my existence, that threatens my happiness. So now what is the state of the mind? The mind is filled with raga dwesha. What will be the natural consequence? The natural consequence is wherever the mind is filled with likes and dislikes, such a mind will always experience delusion, which is called as Moha. Moha. Moha means delusion. What do you mean delusion? The inability to see what is is called delusion. You see what is not there, you don't see what is there. This is called delusion. A mind which is filled with raga dwesha will be a mind which will be deluded. They go together. Greater the raga dwesha, greater will be the delusion. And this is exactly what Arjuna is experiencing. What do you mean raga dwesha leads to delusion? Some examples will make it clear. What is delusion? The inability to see the truth as it is is called delusion. Why are you unable to see the truth? You are unable to see the truth because raga colors the reality. Another meaning of raga is color. In Sanskrit, this is another meaning, dye, D Y E. Raga means that also. We are not talking of musical raga. Raga has so many meanings. In music also there is a raga, not that. So now a mind which is filled with raga dwesha will color your mind and with a colored mind, You will not be able to see the truth as it is. What kind of truth you will see? You will see a colored truth. You will see a distorted truth. Examples will make it clear now. What is the example? So here is a judge. He's supposed to judge impartially. Now his own son, his most beloved son has been caught by the police as a criminal and now he's standing there. Now the father, the judge, he has to judge. But he loves his son extremely. So now naturally what happens? Now this raga will start interfering with his sense of impartiality, sense of judgement. So what will he say? To err is human, to forgive is divine. Why? Because this is my son. Now see, this is called Moha, you know. You tend to analyze a situation compelled by your raga dweshas. This is what happens. Raga dwesha paralyzes your intellect, paralyzes your discriminating ability. So this Arjuna disease is a disease which we are all suffering from somewhere or the other. A teacher who is correcting the papers. And now as she is correcting, she comes to know that oh this paper is my own son's paper. Now as a teacher what is she supposed to do? She has to give marks impartially, if the answer is right, she should give full marks, if the answer is wrong, she should not give marks. Now, Through the handwriting she has understood 10th, what you call, standard exam paper. Through the handwriting she understood this is my son's paper. Now what will she tend to do? She will tend to give more marks, isn't it? This is my son. Now see the conflict here. The teacher in me wants to be impartial, the mother in me wants to be partial towards my own son. Now there is a conflict here. Now this is called Arjuna disease. Attachment towards my son is not allowing me to remain impartial. That's why in Chinmaya Mission we never allow these parents as judges during Bhagavad Gita chanting competition. You understand? If the judge is his mother, her child is chanting Bhagavad Gita. It is said wherever, what is that? Where love is thick, fault is thin. is a saying. Where love is thick, fault is thin. So naturally when she hears her child chanting Bhagavad Gita, she will not see any of these faults, only nice nice things she will hear. This is the handicap of an intellect which is suffering from the virus of attachment. It just wants to listen what is pleasing to it. It just wants to see what is pleasing to it. It sees the truth in a distorted way. It sees the truth according to its own convenience. Another example. Mother child example is the best example because the mother is the one who is so attached to the child. She does everything foolish for the child. So there is this drama competition going on. Her child is there as one of the character in the drama. So in the drama there is this king, there is this queen, there is this minister, there is this hero, heroine, so many things are there and her child is there in a corner. Holding one spear, he is the gatekeeper in a corner. He has no role. His only role is to hold this. Now this mother is clicking what you call that camera. Now everybody has got a camera now. So now the mother is focusing, where will she focus? Will she focus the center stage where all important things are happening? No, automatically, helplessly, spontaneously. Her camera will go towards that fellow who is standing in the corner, doing nothing, looking here there. Isn't it? Who will be the center character in her camera? Not the king who is sitting in the central stage, but the fellow who is in the corner. After the drama you ask that mother, Amma, what was the story about in that drama? She is not aware. The only thing I know is this fellow is there standing as a guard. Maybe he is the most important fellow. Are you able to understand how this raga makes you moodha, the one who is having moha is called moodha. Raga, intense attachment makes you paralyzed, you are helpless. You are not able to think clearly. What is very clearly visible for others, you are not able to see. not able to see. You are in your own hallucination, your own imagination. You have created a castle of foolishness where you are the king. This is Moha. You are seeing what is not there, you are not seeing what is there. And this is exactly what Arjuna is facing now. He is actually a Kshatriya. What is his duty? To fight against unrighteousness, to fight for righteousness, that is his duty. He has come to the war field as a Kshatriya, as an army man. He has not come to the war field as a family man. Now what is he doing? His all arguments are the arguments of a family man, not as an army man. See that. All of us we have different roles to play in the society. Some roles are higher, some roles are lower. The roles which are connected to the nation, those roles are higher roles. For example, Arjuna, his higher role is the role in which he has to discharge the responsibility, keeping in mind. The citizens of the nation, that's a bigger role. The army role is a bigger role, family role is a smaller role. When there is a conflict between the bigger role and the smaller role, which one should you adopt? Whenever there is a conflict. Now exactly that is happening in Arjuna's case. The family role is coming in conflict with the bigger role, the army role. Army role asks him to fight, family role asks him to withdraw. Now which one should he take? You should take the bigger role always. You must sacrifice the lower for the sake of the higher. Just like the teacher who is correcting the paper. The teacher in her wants to be impartial, the mother in her wants to be partial. Which role should she take? The teacher role or a mother role? She has to take the teacher role because that role is bigger. That is going to influence the majority of the society in the in the society, isn't it? All of us, we have this conflict in life. This is not something which Arjuna alone is facing. So now what is the mistake Arjuna has done? Now he is acting and thinking. remaining in the family role, not remaining in the army role. This is the mistake he's doing. Higher is discarded for the sake of the lower. So that is why always you will see this term, Swajanam, Swajanam. He's constantly saying the same thing, Swajanam. Swajanam means what? My people. I am theirs, they are mine. All these things show how much attached he was, how because of attachment his thinking has gone off. Very many times we experience this. And now, what is the result of this Moha? Moha will force you to do Paradharma. This is the next one. What is not your duty, you will start doing it. What is your duty, you will start escaping from it. You will not do it. Svadharma you will not do, Moha will force you to do paradharma and that is exactly what Arjuna is doing. Arjuna is saying I will not fight, it is far better if I take go and take bhiksha. Are bhiksha is not your job. Bhiksha is meant for sanyasis. Bhiksha for you is paradharma. What is your swadharma? Your swadharma is to fight, not take bhiksha. It is far better if I go and take bhiksha and live on alms, fool. You are doing paradharma now. A brahmachari has a right to take bhiksha. A sanyasi has a right to take bhiksha. A grihastha has no right to take bhiksha. Especially a kshatriya has absolutely no right to take bhiksha. Now he's saying, I will do that. See that? It is paradharma. Suppose there is a person, his higher officer, he's forcing him to become corrupt, asking him to take bribes, forcing him to take all the improper, illegal, immoral measures. What should he do? The higher officer is asking him to do. Now this person thinks the pros and cons. If I don't listen to him, if I displease him, what will happen? I will lose my job. If I lose my job, how will I take care of my wife and children? You see that? Very many times people come and describe. It's a very, what you call, prestigious job. Thousands and thousands of people are waiting to get that job and you have got it. And unfortunately, you have a boss. What kind of boss? Who is corrupt and who wants you to assist him in his corruption? What will you do? Now suddenly you also will have Arjuna disease. But in majority of the cases there is no disease because happily the person joins hands with him. Then there is no disease then. If you are compromising, then there is no disease. The moment you try to oppose it, go against it. No, come what may, I'm not going to compromise with a higher principle, even if the job goes away, it doesn't matter. Lord will take care. If this is your thing, hats off to you. But normally what do we do? Moha is there. If I lose my job, how will I take care of my wife and children? So what to do? Better assist him. Then comes Paradharma. See that? Ajnana. Next one? Dehatma bhavana. Next one? Raga. Next one? Moha, raga dwesha together. Raga dwesha, then moha, next what? Paradharma. What should be the next? The next is choicelessly shoka, sorrow. And this is what Arjuna is facing now. See the sequence. When you do what you are not supposed to do, when you compromise with the higher principles of life, when you are unrighteous, helplessly, You will experience only one emotion and that is sorrow. You have no choice. Anyone who compromises with higher values has no choice but to remain miserable. Shoka is the consequence of the wrong actions, of the wrong decisions, of the wrong analysis of life. The end result is Shoka. A person who lives a corrupt life, immoral life, illegal life, look at his condition. Shoka at three levels, adhyatmika level, adhibhautika level, adhidaivika level, all the levels he will experience only sorrow. When you are corrupt, your own mind is not at peace. That is selfish yoga. When you are corrupt, someday or the other you will be caught. The higher officer is caught along with you are also caught. So what happens? At the aadhi bhautika level also you experience shoka. You are put into jail. All your name, fame, everything gone. In the newspaper, big, big letters your name come. What is that? Nothing but shoka only. Humiliation, isn't it? And there are some news channels, thousands and thousands of time they will show the same thing again and again, again and again. They will ensure that the people never forget even after their death. See that? Just imagine the amount of humiliation, that pain which that person is suffering when he sees all this. Shoka at the mind level, Shoka at the worldly level, of course after death also Shoka alone because he has done all adharmic actions. Isn't it? What will be the result?
